# Authoring .drawio XML

Read this **before hand-writing any `.drawio` XML** (workflow step 3). Skip it when a bundled generator writes the XML for you (`autolayout.py` + importers, `seqlayout.py`).

### File skeleton

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<mxfile host="drawio" version="26.0.0">
  <diagram name="Page-1">
    <mxGraphModel>
      <root>
        <mxCell id="0" />
        <mxCell id="1" parent="0" />
        <!-- user shapes start at id="2" -->
      </root>
    </mxGraphModel>
  </diagram>
</mxfile>
```

**Rules:**

- `id="0"` and `id="1"` are required root cells — never omit them
- User shapes start at `id="2"` and increment sequentially
- All shapes have `parent="1"` (unless inside a container — then use container's id)
- All text uses `html=1` in style for proper rendering
- **Never use `--` inside XML comments** — it's illegal per XML spec and causes parse errors
- Escape special characters in attribute values: `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`
- **Multi-line text in labels:** use `
` for line breaks inside `value` attributes (not literal `\n`). Example: `value="Line 1
Line 2"`

### Shape types (vertex)

| Style keyword | Use for |
| -------------- | --------- |
| `rounded=0` | plain rectangle (default) |
| `rounded=1` | rounded rectangle — services, modules |
| `ellipse;` | circles/ovals — start/end, databases |
| `rhombus;` | diamond — decision points |
| `shape=mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon;` | AWS icons |
| `shape=cylinder3;` | cylinder — databases |
| `swimlane;` | group/container with title bar |

For **vendor/branded icons** (AWS/Azure/GCP/Cisco/Kubernetes) and any non-trivial shape, don't guess the `shape=mxgraph.*` name — a wrong name renders as a blank box. Run `python3 <this-skill-dir>/scripts/shapesearch.py "<keywords>"` to get the exact official style + size, or see `references/shapes.md` for the hand-writable cheatsheet. For **AI/LLM brand logos** (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, …), which draw.io has none of, use `python3 <this-skill-dir>/scripts/aiicons.py "<brand>"`.

### Required properties

```xml
<!-- Rectangle / rounded box -->
<mxCell id="2" value="Label" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;" vertex="1" parent="1">
  <mxGeometry x="100" y="100" width="160" height="60" as="geometry" />
</mxCell>

<!-- Cylinder (database) -->
<mxCell id="3" value="DB" style="shape=cylinder3;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;fontColor=#333333;" vertex="1" parent="1">
  <mxGeometry x="350" y="100" width="120" height="80" as="geometry" />
</mxCell>

<!-- Diamond (decision) -->
<mxCell id="4" value="Check?" style="rhombus;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;" vertex="1" parent="1">
  <mxGeometry x="100" y="220" width="160" height="80" as="geometry" />
</mxCell>
```

### Containers and groups

For architecture diagrams with nested elements, use draw.io's parent-child containment — do **not** just place shapes on top of larger shapes.

| Type | Style | When to use |
| ------ | ------- | ------------- |
| **Group** (invisible) | `group;pointerEvents=0;` | No visual border needed, container has no connections |
| **Swimlane** (titled) | `swimlane;startSize=30;` | Container needs a visible title bar, or container itself has connections |
| **Custom container** | Add `container=1;pointerEvents=0;` to any shape | Any shape acting as a container without its own connections |

**Key rules:**

- Add `pointerEvents=0;` to container styles that should not capture connections between children
- Children set `parent="containerId"` and use coordinates **relative to the container**

```xml
<!-- Swimlane container -->
<mxCell id="svc1" value="User Service" style="swimlane;startSize=30;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;" vertex="1" parent="1">
  <mxGeometry x="100" y="100" width="300" height="200" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
<!-- Child inside container — coordinates relative to parent -->
<mxCell id="api1" value="REST API" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="svc1">
  <mxGeometry x="20" y="40" width="120" height="60" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
<mxCell id="db1" value="Database" style="shape=cylinder3;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="svc1">
  <mxGeometry x="160" y="40" width="120" height="60" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
```

### Connector (edge)

**CRITICAL:** Every edge `mxCell` must contain a `<mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" />` child element. Self-closing edge cells (`<mxCell ... edge="1" ... />`) are **invalid** and will not render. Always use the expanded form.

```xml
<!-- Directed arrow — always include rounded, orthogonalLoop, jettySize for clean routing -->
<mxCell id="10" value="" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;" edge="1" parent="1" source="2" target="3">
  <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" />
</mxCell>

<!-- Arrow with label + explicit entry/exit points to control direction -->
<mxCell id="11" value="HTTP/REST" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="2" target="4">
  <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" />
</mxCell>

<!-- Arrow with waypoints — use when edge must route around other shapes -->
<mxCell id="12" value="" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;" edge="1" parent="1" source="3" target="5">
  <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry">
    <Array as="points">
      <mxPoint x="500" y="50" />
    </Array>
  </mxGeometry>
</mxCell>
```

**Edge style rules:**

- **Animated connectors:** add `flowAnimation=1;` to any edge style to show a moving dot animation along the arrow. Works in SVG export and draw.io desktop — ideal for data-flow and pipeline diagrams. Example: `style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;flowAnimation=1;rounded=1;..."`
- **Always** include `rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto` — these enable smart routing that avoids overlaps
- Pin `exitX/exitY/entryX/entryY` on every edge when a node has 2+ connections — distributes lines across the shape perimeter. `scripts/edgeports.py <file>` does this for a whole diagram: it picks the side facing each peer and spreads that side's edges over even slots ordered by the far endpoint, so they don't stack or cross at the boundary. It skips ends you pinned by hand and is idempotent
- Add `<Array as="points">` waypoints when an edge must detour around an intermediate shape
- **Leave room for arrowheads:** the final straight segment between the last bend and the target shape must be ≥20px long. If too short, the arrowhead overlaps the bend and looks broken. Fix by increasing node spacing or adding explicit waypoints
- **libavoid obstacle-avoiding routing (editor-side, draw.io ≥ 30):** draw.io has a newer connector router that recomputes edge paths to run *around* shapes (fanning out parallel edges) without moving any node. It runs interactively in the draw.io desktop editor (or via jgraph's MCP app-server `routing:"libavoid"`) — it is **not** a headless CLI flag. Passing `--layout libavoid` opens a modal `Unknown layout:` error dialog and hangs the run (jgraph's own drawio-mcp plugin docs claim the CLI flag works — verified hang on 30.2.6, don't trust it); the CLI `--layout` values are ELK *node* layout presets, a different thing (see `mermaid-authoring.md`). For CLI-authored files keep the orthogonal rules above; if a dense diagram still has crossings after export, open the `.drawio` in draw.io desktop once and let libavoid re-route. Don't stack it on an ELK `--layout` pass — pick one router, not both.

### Distributing connections on a shape

When multiple edges connect to the same shape, assign different entry/exit points to prevent stacking:

| Position | exitX/entryX | exitY/entryY | Use when |
| ---------- | ------------- | ------------- | ---------- |
| Top center | 0.5 | 0 | connecting to node above |
| Top-left | 0.25 | 0 | 2nd connection from top |
| Top-right | 0.75 | 0 | 3rd connection from top |
| Right center | 1 | 0.5 | connecting to node on right |
| Bottom center | 0.5 | 1 | connecting to node below |
| Left center | 0 | 0.5 | connecting to node on left |

**Rule:** if a shape has N connections on one side, space them evenly (e.g., 3 connections on bottom → exitX = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75)

### Color palette (fillColor / strokeColor)

*Used only when no user style preset is active (see `references/style-presets.md` → "Applying a preset").*

| Color name | fillColor | strokeColor | Use for |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | --------- |
| Blue | `#dae8fc` | `#6c8ebf` | services, clients |
| Green | `#d5e8d4` | `#82b366` | success, databases |
| Yellow | `#fff2cc` | `#d6b656` | queues, decisions |
| Orange | `#ffe6cc` | `#d79b00` | gateways, APIs |
| Red/Pink | `#f8cecc` | `#b85450` | errors, alerts |
| Grey | `#f5f5f5` | `#666666` | external/neutral |
| Purple | `#e1d5e7` | `#9673a6` | security, auth |

### Legend (auto-generate from the palette)

When a diagram uses 3+ semantic colors, add a legend so the color coding is self-explanatory. Generate it mechanically from the roles actually present — never invent legend entries that aren't in the diagram:

```xml
<!-- Legend container: place in a corner clear of the diagram (e.g. below-left) -->
<mxCell id="legend" value="Legend" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#666666;verticalAlign=top;fontStyle=1;" vertex="1" parent="1">
  <mxGeometry x="40" y="720" width="180" height="110" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
<!-- One swatch + label pair per used role, 24px row pitch, children of the legend -->
<mxCell id="leg1" value="" style="rounded=0;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;" vertex="1" parent="legend">
  <mxGeometry x="10" y="30" width="30" height="16" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
<mxCell id="leg1t" value="Service" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;" vertex="1" parent="legend">
  <mxGeometry x="50" y="28" width="120" height="20" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
```

Rules: swatch colors come from the active palette (preset or the table above) with the **role name** as the label (Service, Database, Queue, …); height = `30 + 24 × rows`; the legend is a container (`parent="legend"`, relative coordinates); skip it entirely for single-color diagrams.

### Layout tips

**Spacing — scale with complexity:**

| Diagram complexity | Nodes | Horizontal gap | Vertical gap |
| ------------------- | ------- | ---------------- | -------------- |
| Simple | ≤5 | 200px | 150px |
| Medium | 6–10 | 280px | 200px |
| Complex | >10 | 350px | 250px |

**Routing corridors:** between shape rows/columns, leave an extra ~80px empty corridor where edges can route without crossing shapes. Never place a shape in a gap that edges need to traverse.

**Grid alignment:** snap all `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` values to **multiples of 10** — this ensures shapes align cleanly on draw.io's default grid and makes manual editing easier.

**General rules:**

- Plan a grid before assigning x/y coordinates — sketch node positions on paper/mentally first
- Group related nodes in the same horizontal or vertical band
- Use `swimlane` cells for logical grouping with visible borders
- Place heavily-connected "hub" nodes centrally so edges radiate outward instead of crossing
- To force straight vertical connections, pin entry/exit points explicitly on edges:
  `exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0`
- Always center-align a child node under its parent (same center x) to avoid diagonal routing
- **Event bus pattern**: place Kafka/bus nodes in the **center of the service row**, not below — services on either side can reach it with short horizontal arrows (`exitX=1` left side, `exitX=0` right side), eliminating all line crossings

- Pin `exitX/exitY/entryX/entryY` on every edge when a node has 2+ connections — distributes lines across the shape perimeter. `scripts/edgeports.py <file>` does this for a whole diagram: it picks the side facing each peer and spreads that side's edges over even slots ordered by the far endpoint, so they don't stack or cross at the boundary. It skips ends you pinned by hand and is idempotent
- Add `<Array as="points">` waypoints when an edge must detour around an intermediate shape
- **Leave room for arrowheads:** the final straight segment between the last bend and the target shape must be ≥20px long. If too short, the arrowhead overlaps the bend and looks broken. Fix by increasing node spacing or adding explicit waypoints
- **libavoid obstacle-avoiding routing (editor-side, draw.io ≥ 30):** draw.io has a newer connector router that recomputes edge paths to run *around* shapes (fanning out parallel edges) without moving any node. It runs interactively in the draw.io desktop editor (or via jgraph's MCP app-server `routing:"libavoid"`) — it is **not** a headless CLI flag. Passing `--layout libavoid` opens a modal `Unknown layout:` error dialog and hangs the run (jgraph's own drawio-mcp plugin docs claim the CLI flag works — verified hang on 30.2.6, don't trust it); the CLI `--layout` values are ELK *node* layout presets, a different thing (see `mermaid-authoring.md`). For CLI-authored files keep the orthogonal rules above; if a dense diagram still has crossings after export, open the `.drawio` in draw.io desktop once and let libavoid re-route. Don't stack it on an ELK `--layout` pass — pick one router, not both.

### Distributing connections on a shape

When multiple edges connect to the same shape, assign different entry/exit points to prevent stacking:

| Position | exitX/entryX | exitY/entryY | Use when |
| ---------- | ------------- | ------------- | ---------- |
| Top center | 0.5 | 0 | connecting to node above |
| Top-left | 0.25 | 0 | 2nd connection from top |
| Top-right | 0.75 | 0 | 3rd connection from top |
| Right center | 1 | 0.5 | connecting to node on right |
| Bottom center | 0.5 | 1 | connecting to node below |
| Left center | 0 | 0.5 | connecting to node on left |

**Rule:** if a shape has N connections on one side, space them evenly (e.g., 3 connections on bottom → exitX = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75)

### Color palette (fillColor / strokeColor)

*Used only when no user style preset is active (see `references/style-presets.md` → "Applying a preset").*

| Color name | fillColor | strokeColor | Use for |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | --------- |
| Blue | `#dae8fc` | `#6c8ebf` | services, clients |
| Green | `#d5e8d4` | `#82b366` | success, databases |
| Yellow | `#fff2cc` | `#d6b656` | queues, decisions |
| Orange | `#ffe6cc` | `#d79b00` | gateways, APIs |
| Red/Pink | `#f8cecc` | `#b85450` | errors, alerts |
| Grey | `#f5f5f5` | `#666666` | external/neutral |
| Purple | `#e1d5e7` | `#9673a6` | security, auth |

### Legend (auto-generate from the palette)

When a diagram uses 3+ semantic colors, add a legend so the color coding is self-explanatory. Generate it mechanically from the roles actually present — never invent legend entries that aren't in the diagram:

```xml
<!-- Legend container: place in a corner clear of the diagram (e.g. below-left) -->
<mxCell id="legend" value="Legend" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#666666;verticalAlign=top;fontStyle=1;" vertex="1" parent="1">
  <mxGeometry x="40" y="720" width="180" height="110" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
<!-- One swatch + label pair per used role, 24px row pitch, children of the legend -->
<mxCell id="leg1" value="" style="rounded=0;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;" vertex="1" parent="legend">
  <mxGeometry x="10" y="30" width="30" height="16" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
<mxCell id="leg1t" value="Service" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;" vertex="1" parent="legend">
  <mxGeometry x="50" y="28" width="120" height="20" as="geometry"/>
</mxCell>
```

Rules: swatch colors come from the active palette (preset or the table above) with the **role name** as the label (Service, Database, Queue, …); height = `30 + 24 × rows`; the legend is a container (`parent="legend"`, relative coordinates); skip it entirely for single-color diagrams.

### Layout tips

**Spacing — scale with complexity:**

| Diagram complexity | Nodes | Horizontal gap | Vertical gap |
| ------------------- | ------- | ---------------- | -------------- |
| Simple | ≤5 | 200px | 150px |
| Medium | 6–10 | 280px | 200px |
| Complex | >10 | 350px | 250px |

**Routing corridors:** between shape rows/columns, leave an extra ~80px empty corridor where edges can route without crossing shapes. Never place a shape in a gap that edges need to traverse.

**Grid alignment:** snap all `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` values to **multiples of 10** — this ensures shapes align cleanly on draw.io's default grid and makes manual editing easier.

**General rules:**

- Plan a grid before assigning x/y coordinates — sketch node positions on paper/mentally first
- Group related nodes in the same horizontal or vertical band
- Use `swimlane` cells for logical grouping with visible borders
- Place heavily-connected "hub" nodes centrally so edges radiate outward instead of crossing
- To force straight vertical connections, pin entry/exit points explicitly on edges:
  `exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0`
- Always center-align a child node under its parent (same center x) to avoid diagonal routing
- **Event bus pattern**: place Kafka/bus nodes in the **center of the service row**, not below — services on either side can reach it with short horizontal arrows (`exitX=1` left side, `exitX=0` right side), eliminating all line crossings

# Architecture overview

Alloq is a resource planning app for software teams. It is written in Python with
[Reflex](https://reflex.dev) 0.10.0, which builds a React frontend from Python code
and runs the event handlers in a Python backend. The data lives in PostgreSQL. The
same code runs as a web app and as a macOS desktop app.

This page describes the system from the outside in. It uses the C4 levels:

- **Context.** Who uses Alloq and which other systems it talks to.
- **Containers.** The programs that run and the data store.
- **Components.** The Python packages inside the app.

The last section follows one request from a page to the database. The
[layers page](./layers.md) then explains each layer in the code.

## System context

Four kinds of people use Alloq. The personas come from the roles in
[`roles.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/roles.py)
(`PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE`, `EMPLOYEE_ROLE`) and the admin switch of appkit-user.

- **Administrator.** An appkit user with the admin switch. Administrators can do
  everything, including the pages under "Administration".
- **Project manager.** A user with the role `project_manager` ("Projektmanager").
  Project managers read and edit planning, projects and team, but they have no
  administration.
- **Employee.** A user with the role `employee` ("Mitarbeiter" [employee]).
  Employees can only read the projects page and the resource planning.
- **Desktop user.** Any of the three above who uses the desktop app. The desktop
  user signs in with Microsoft Entra ID and connects to Postgres with a personal
  token.

![System context: users, Alloq, Microsoft Entra ID and PostgreSQL](../diagrams/system-context.drawio.png)

[Editable source: system-context.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/system-context.drawio)

The base configuration
[`configuration/config.yaml`](../../configuration/config.yaml) lists one OAuth
provider, `azure`. A GitHub provider is in the file but commented out. The desktop
sign-in is described on the [desktop page](./desktop.md).

content.content:
sign-in is described on the [desktop page](./desktop.md).

## Containers

Alloq has two ways to run the same Python code.

- **Web app.** The Reflex backend runs on a server (backend port `3030` in
  `config.yaml`, `workers: 2`). It serves the compiled frontend below the path
  `/alloq` (`frontend_path`). Users open it in a browser. The browser talks to the
  backend over a websocket. Every click that needs data sends an event over this
  websocket to a state class in the backend.
- **Desktop app.** A Tauri shell in [`tauri/`](../../tauri/src-tauri/src/main.rs)
  starts the same Python backend inside the app process. `main.rs` runs it on a
  background thread bound to `127.0.0.1:18442` (`BACKEND_PORT`) and shows the
  prebuilt frontend in a webview. The app carries no secrets. Each person signs in
  with Entra ID and connects to Postgres with their own token.
- **PostgreSQL.** One database holds the Alloq tables and the appkit-user tables.
  The web app connects with the credentials from the `secret:` entries in
  `config.yaml`. The desktop app connects with the Entra token of the signed-in
  person.

![Deployment: the web app and the desktop app](../diagrams/deployment-modes.drawio.png)

[Editable source: deployment-modes.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/deployment-modes.drawio)

The configuration profiles that select these modes are listed in the
[configuration reference](../reference/configuration.md).

![Alloq system architecture: planners and admins, the Tauri desktop shell, the Reflex app and PostgreSQL](../images/alloq-system.svg)

The diagram shows the same containers, with the components inside the Reflex app.

## Components: the package split

The code is a uv workspace. The host app and four packages are members. The
workspace is declared in [`pyproject.toml`](../../pyproject.toml) under
`[tool.uv.workspace]` with `members = ["components/*"]`.

| Package | Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host app | [`app/`](../../app/app.py) | Entry point `app/app.py`, admin pages in `app/pages/`, the sidebar in `app/components/sidebar.py`, desktop code in `app/desktop/`, configuration in `app/configuration.py` |
| `alloq-commons` | [`components/alloq-commons`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/__init__.py) | Entities, models, repositories, shared services (`utilization.py`, `quick_project.py`, `daily_rate_pricing.py`), shared UI (`shell.py`, `list_view.py`, `toolbar.py`, `excel_grid/`), `roles.py`, `access.py`, `theme.py`, and the department, role, daily rate and holiday states |
| `alloq-team` | [`components/alloq-team`](../../components/alloq-team/src/alloq_team/pages.py) | Team page (`/team`), employee table, cards, inspector and form, `TeamState` |
| `alloq-project` | [`components/alloq-project`](../../components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/pages.py) | Projects page (`/projects`), planning page (`/` and `/plan`), planning grid, Gantt view, plan modal, forecast and plan distribution services |
| `alloq-dashboard` | [`components/alloq-dashboard`](../../components/alloq-dashboard/src/alloq_dashboard/pages.py) | Dashboard page (`/dashboard`), KPI cards, portfolio, drill-down drawers, aggregation services |

Each feature package has the same folders: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`
and a `pages.py` with a page factory. The host app calls every page factory once in
[`app/app.py`](../../app/app.py) and passes it the sidebar.

All packages also use the appkit libraries from PyPI: `appkit-commons` (database
session, base repository, configuration, service registry), `appkit-user` (users,

## Containers

Alloq has two ways to run the same Python code.

- **Web app.** The Reflex backend runs on a server (backend port `3030` in
  `config.yaml`, `workers: 2`). It serves the compiled frontend below the path
  `/alloq` (`frontend_path`). Users open it in a browser. The browser talks to the
  backend over a websocket. Every click that needs data sends an event over this
  websocket to a state class in the backend.
- **Desktop app.** A Tauri shell in [`tauri/`](../../tauri/src-tauri/src/main.rs)
  starts the same Python backend inside the app process. `main.rs` runs it on a
  background thread bound to `127.0.0.1:18442` (`BACKEND_PORT`) and shows the
  prebuilt frontend in a webview. The app carries no secrets. Each person signs in
  with Entra ID and connects to Postgres with their own token.
- **PostgreSQL.** One database holds the Alloq tables and the appkit-user tables.
  The web app connects with the credentials from the `secret:` entries in
  `config.yaml`. The desktop app connects with the Entra token of the signed-in
  person.

[Editable source: deployment-modes.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/deployment-modes.drawio)

[configuration reference](../reference/configuration.md).

# Security and access

Alloq uses the library appkit-user for users, sign-in and sessions. Alloq adds its
own access levels on top. This page explains both parts and the tests that keep
them in place. The desktop sign-in with Entra ID is on the
[desktop page](./desktop.md).

## Overview

A request passes several checks. Each check has a different job.

![Request guards from the browser to the database](../diagrams/request-guards.drawio.png)

[Editable source: request-guards.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/request-guards.drawio)

Only the handler guard protects the data. The other checks decide what a user sees
and send users without a session to the login page. The docstring of
[`tests/test_handler_authorization.py`](../../tests/test_handler_authorization.py)
states the reason: page guards only affect rendering, and event handlers run over
the websocket regardless.

## Sign-in

### Login page

[`create_login_page`](../../app/pages/login.py) registers the route `/login` with
the title "Anmelden" [sign in]. Its `on_load` runs
`LoginState.clear_session_storage_token`. On the desktop, `desktop_handlers` adds
`SplashState.finish`.

The web variant of `login_view` shows:

- A form with "E-Mail" and "Passwort" [password]. The button "Anmelden" submits it
  to `LoginState.login_with_password` of appkit-user.
-----LAYERS
---

# Layers

Every feature in Alloq is built from the same layers. This page explains each layer
and shows it on one feature, the departments page at `/admin/departments`
("Abteilungen" [departments]). The departments slice is small and touches every
layer, so it is a good model when you add a new feature.

Paths below are relative to this page. `commons` means
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons`.

| Layer | What it does | Departments file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | SQLAlchemy table mapping | [`entities/department.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/entities/department.py) |
| Model | Pydantic read model and write model | [`models/department.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/models/department.py) |
| Repository | Database queries for one entity | [`repositories/department_repository.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/repositories/department_repository.py) |
| Service | Calculations without UI (none for departments) | see [Service](#service) |
| State | Reflex state with guarded event handlers | [`state/department_states.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/state/department_states.py) |
| Component | UI built from `appkit_mantine` | [`components/department.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/department.py) |
| Page | Page factory with route, toolbar and `on_load` | [`app/pages/departments.py`](../../app/pages/departments.py) |
| Registration | Page factory call and sidebar entry | [`app/app.py`](../../app/app.py), [`app/components/sidebar.py`](../../app/components/sidebar.py) |
| Migration | Hand-written Alembic file | [`2026_10_18_departments.py`](../../alembic/versions/2026_10_18_departments.py) |
| Tests | State, model and component tests | [`test_departments.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py) |

![Layers for the department example](../diagrams/layers-department.drawio.png)

[Editable source: layers-department.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/layers-department.drawio)

## Entity

An entity maps one table. Entities live in `commons/entities/` and are exported
from `commons/entities/__init__.py`.

`DepartmentEntity` maps the table `departments`. It inherits `Entity` and `Base`
from `appkit_commons.database.entities`. `Entity` adds three columns to every table:

- `id`, an integer primary key with autoincrement.
- `created`, a timestamp with time zone, set by the database (`server_default`).
- `updated`, a timestamp with time zone, set on insert and on every update.

# Desktop app

The desktop app is a Tauri app for macOS with the Python backend built in. It uses
the library reflex-desktop. It uses the same central Postgres database as the web
app, and it carries no secrets. Each person signs in with Microsoft Entra ID and
connects to Postgres with their own access token.

This page is the English version of [`spec/desktop.md`](../../spec/desktop.md),
checked against `app/desktop/`, `tauri/` and `scripts/desktop.py`. Where the two
differ, this page follows the code.

## How the app runs

![Desktop app architecture](../diagrams/desktop-architecture.drawio.png)

[Editable source: desktop-architecture.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/desktop-architecture.drawio)

- [`main.rs`](../../tauri/src-tauri/src/main.rs) starts the Python ASGI backend
  inside the app process through PyO3, on a background thread bound to
  `127.0.0.1:18442` (`BACKEND_PORT`). The webview shows the prebuilt frontend and
  talks to that backend.
- The bundle contains a Python interpreter (`python/`), the packages
  (`site-packages/`) and the app payload (`app/`). They are listed under
  `bundle.resources` in [`tauri.conf.json`](../../tauri/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json).
- `rxconfig.py` adds the `DesktopPlugin` from reflex-desktop only when
  `is_desktop()` is true (`desktop_plugins`). Inside the bundle, `cors_origins`
  allows only the webview origins `tauri://localhost`, `http://tauri.localhost`
  and `http://127.0.0.1:18442` to open the event socket.
- The window is 1440 by 900 pixels, at least 1100 by 700, with the title bar style
  `Overlay`. The sidebar of the app shell leaves its top row free for the window
  buttons.

### When the app counts as desktop

[`is_desktop()`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/desktop.py)
returns true when `ALLOQ_DESKTOP=1` is set or when `REFLEX_DESKTOP_APP_ROOT` is
set. The Tauri host sets the second variable in the bundle.

[`activate_desktop_profile`](../../app/desktop/profile.py) runs in
`app/__init__.py` before the configuration is loaded. It adds the profile
`desktop` last to `PROFILES`, so it overrides every server value. When
`ALLOQ_FAKE_ENTRA_EMAIL` is set and the app does not run in the bundle, it also
adds `desktop_fake`.

### The desktop profile

[`configuration/config.desktop.yaml`](../../configuration/config.desktop.yaml)
sets:

- `backend_port: 18442`, which must match `BACKEND_PORT` in `main.rs`, and
  `workers: 1`.
- A database with an empty `username` and `password`, because both come from the
  Entra sign-in. `ssl_mode: require`, `pool_size: 2`, `max_overflow: 3`.
- An empty `encryption_key`. The comment says that only the stored OAuth tokens of
  appkit are encrypted and the desktop app never touches them.
- `oauth_providers: []`. The web OAuth flows need client secrets, and the desktop
  app has its own sign-in.
- `app.desktop` with `tenant_id`, `client_id` and `db_role` (see
  [`DesktopConfig`](../../app/desktop/config.py)).

Desktop variants in the UI:

- The login page shows only "Mit Microsoft anmelden" [sign in with Microsoft]
  (`_desktop_sign_in` in [`app/pages/login.py`](../../app/pages/login.py)).
- Every page shows a splash screen until its `on_load` handlers are done
  (`SplashState.finish` in
  [`splash.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/splash.py)).
- The sidebar uses `DesktopLoginState.sign_out` to sign out.
- The users page shows the database access button (see below).

## Sign-in flow

![Sequence: desktop sign-in with Microsoft](../diagrams/desktop-sign-in-sequence.drawio.png)

[Editable source: desktop-sign-in-sequence.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/desktop-sign-in-sequence.drawio)

The steps in [`login_state.py`](../../app/desktop/login_state.py)
(`DesktopLoginState.sign_in_with_microsoft`, a background handler):

1. `microsoft_account` first tries the cached account from the macOS Keychain
   (service `alloq`, account `entra-token-cache`). When there is none, MSAL opens
   the sign-in in the default browser. This is the authorization code flow with
   PKCE and a redirect to `http://localhost`. The browser sign-in may take up to
   `sign_in_timeout` seconds, 300 by default.
2. `reset_connections` closes all pooled connections, because they carry the
   identity of the previous user.
3. Every new database connection gets the user and token of the signed-in person.
   `install_db_auth` in [`entra.py`](../../app/desktop/entra.py) registers a

own access levels on top. This page explains both parts and the tests that keep
them in place. The desktop sign-in with Entra ID is on the
[desktop page](./desktop.md).

## Overview

A request passes several checks. Each check has a different job.

![Request guards from the browser to the database](../diagrams/request-guards.drawio.png)

[Editable source: request-guards.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/request-guards.drawio)

Only the handler guard protects the data. The other checks decide what a user sees
and send users without a session to the login page. The docstring of
[`tests/test_handler_authorization.py`](../../tests/test_handler_authorization.py)
states the reason: page guards only affect rendering, and event handlers run over
the websocket regardless.

## Sign-in

### Login page

[`create_login_page`](../../app/pages/login.py) registers the route `/login` with
the title "Anmelden" [sign in]. Its `on_load` runs
`LoginState.clear_session_storage_token`. On the desktop, `desktop_handlers` adds
`SplashState.finish`.

The web variant of `login_view` shows:

- A form with "E-Mail" and "Passwort" [password]. The button "Anmelden" submits it
  to `LoginState.login_with_password` of appkit-user.

# Layers

Every feature in Alloq is built from the same layers. This page explains each layer
and shows it on one feature, the departments page at `/admin/departments`
("Abteilungen" [departments]). The departments slice is small and touches every
layer, so it is a good model when you add a new feature.

Paths below are relative to this page. `commons` means
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons`.

| Layer | What it does | Departments file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | SQLAlchemy table mapping | [`entities/department.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/entities/department.py) |
| Model | Pydantic read model and write model | [`models/department.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/models/department.py) |
| Repository | Database queries for one entity | [`repositories/department_repository.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/repositories/department_repository.py) |
| Service | Calculations without UI (none for departments) | see [Service](#service) |
| State | Reflex state with guarded event handlers | [`state/department_states.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/state/department_states.py) |
| Component | UI built from `appkit_mantine` | [`components/department.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/department.py) |
| Page | Page factory with route, toolbar and `on_load` | [`app/pages/departments.py`](../../app/pages/departments.py) |
| Registration | Page factory call and sidebar entry | [`app/app.py`](../../app/app.py), [`app/components/sidebar.py`](../../app/components/sidebar.py) |
| Migration | Hand-written Alembic file | [`2026_10_18_departments.py`](../../alembic/versions/2026_10_18_departments.py) |
| Tests | State, model and component tests | [`test_departments.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py) |

![Layers for the department example](../diagrams/layers-department.drawio.png)

[Editable source: layers-department.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/layers-department.drawio)

## Entity

An entity maps one table. Entities live in `commons/entities/` and are exported
from `commons/entities/__init__.py`.

`DepartmentEntity` maps the table `departments`. It inherits `Entity` and `Base`
from `appkit_commons.database.entities`. `Entity` adds three columns to every table:

- `id`, an integer primary key with autoincrement.
- `created`, a timestamp with time zone, set by the database (`server_default`).
- `updated`, a timestamp with time zone, set on insert and on every update.

# Desktop app

The desktop app is a Tauri app for macOS with the Python backend built in. It uses
the library reflex-desktop. It uses the same central Postgres database as the web
app, and it carries no secrets. Each person signs in with Microsoft Entra ID and
connects to Postgres with their own access token.

This page is the English version of [`spec/desktop.md`](../../spec/desktop.md),
checked against `app/desktop/`, `tauri/` and `scripts/desktop.py`. Where the two
differ, this page follows the code.

## How the app runs

![Desktop app architecture](../diagrams/desktop-architecture.drawio.png)

[Editable source: desktop-architecture.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/desktop-architecture.drawio)

- [`main.rs`](../../tauri/src-tauri/src/main.rs) starts the Python ASGI backend
  inside the app process through PyO3, on a background thread bound to
  `127.0.0.1:18442` (`BACKEND_PORT`). The webview shows the prebuilt frontend and
  talks to that backend.
- The bundle contains a Python interpreter (`python/`), the packages
  (`site-packages/`) and the app payload (`app/`). They are listed under
  `bundle.resources` in [`tauri.conf.json`](../../tauri/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json).
- `rxconfig.py` adds the `DesktopPlugin` from reflex-desktop only when
  `is_desktop()` is true (`desktop_plugins`). Inside the bundle, `cors_origins`
  allows only the webview origins `tauri://localhost`, `http://tauri.localhost`
  and `http://127.0.0.1:18442` to open the event socket.
- The window is 1440 by 900 pixels, at least 1100 by 700, with the title bar style
  `Overlay`. The sidebar of the app shell leaves its top row free for the window
  buttons.

### When the app counts as desktop

[`is_desktop()`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/desktop.py)
returns true when `ALLOQ_DESKTOP=1` is set or when `REFLEX_DESKTOP_APP_ROOT` is
set. The Tauri host sets the second variable in the bundle.

[`activate_desktop_profile`](../../app/desktop/profile.py) runs in
`app/__init__.py` before the configuration is loaded. It adds the profile
`desktop` last to `PROFILES`, so it overrides every server value. When
`ALLOQ_FAKE_ENTRA_EMAIL` is set and the app does not run in the bundle, it also
adds `desktop_fake`.

### The desktop profile

[`configuration/config.desktop.yaml`](../../configuration/config.desktop.yaml)
sets:

- `backend_port: 18442`, which must match `BACKEND_PORT` in `main.rs`, and
  `workers: 1`.
- A database with an empty `username` and `password`, because both come from the
  Entra sign-in. `ssl_mode: require`, `pool_size: 2`, `max_overflow: 3`.
- An empty `encryption_key`. The comment says that only the stored OAuth tokens of
  appkit are encrypted and the desktop app never touches them.
- `oauth_providers: []`. The web OAuth flows need client secrets, and the desktop
  app has its own sign-in.
- `app.desktop` with `tenant_id`, `client_id` and `db_role` (see
  [`DesktopConfig`](../../app/desktop/config.py)).

Desktop variants in the UI:

- The login page shows only "Mit Microsoft anmelden" [sign in with Microsoft]
  (`_desktop_sign_in` in [`app/pages/login.py`](../../app/pages/login.py)).
- Every page shows a splash screen until its `on_load` handlers are done
  (`SplashState.finish` in
  [`splash.py`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/splash.py)).
- The sidebar uses `DesktopLoginState.sign_out` to sign out.
- The users page shows the database access button (see below).

[Editable source: desktop-sign-in-sequence.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/desktop-sign-in-sequence.drawio)

SQLAlchemy `do_connect` listener that calls `connect_params`. The user is `db_role` when it is set, otherwise the email from the token. The password is the access token. Before sign-in there is no connection, because `connect_params` raises `NotSignedInError`. `app/app.py` installs this listener only when `is_desktop()` is true and the sign-in is an `EntraSignIn`. 4. `allowed_user` checks the schema version with `schema_problem`. When it does not match, sign-in stops with a message. Migrations run only on the server. 5. `allowed_user` finds the Alloq user with the same email, without regard to case (`find_user`). The desktop app does not create users. An unknown email gives the message in `NO_ACCOUNT`, e.g. "Für {email} gibt es kein alloq-Konto. ..." [there is no alloq account for this email]. An inactive or not verified account gives the matching text from `STATUS_MESSAGES`. 6. The handler opens the normal appkit session with `_create_session` and redirects to the page the user asked for, or to the homepage. There is no password login in the desktop app. The docstring of `login_state.py` gives the reason: without a signed-in Microsoft account the app has no database access to check a password against. ### Token renewal and restart - `EntraSignIn` keeps the access token with its expiry. A background thread renews it `REFRESH_MARGIN` (300) seconds before it expires. When renewal fails, it tries again after `RETRY_SECONDS` (60) seconds. - `access_token()` never hands out a token that expires within `EXPIRY_SLACK` (60) seconds. - After a restart, `restore()` brings back the Microsoft account from the Keychain without a browser, as soon as a connection needs it. It tries at most every `RESTORE_INTERVAL` (30) seconds. When the Alloq session is still valid, the user goes on without the login page. ### Sign-out "Abmelden" [sign out] calls `DesktopLoginState.sign_out`. It ends the appkit session (`logout`), removes the Microsoft account from the token cache on this Mac (`EntraSignIn.sign_out`) and closes all database connections (`reset_connections`). ## Schema check [`app/desktop/schema.py`](../../app/desktop/schema.py) holds `KNOWN_REVISIONS`, the Alembic history newest first. `EXPECTED_REVISION` is the first entry. `schema_problem` reads `alembic_version` and returns: - `None` when the database has the expected revision. - A message that the server migration is still missing, when the revision is an older known one. - A message to update the app, when the revision is unknown or empty. After every new migration, add its revision at the front of `KNOWN_REVISIONS`. The test `test_known_revisions_are_the_alembic_history` in [`tests/test_desktop_login.py`](../../tests/test_desktop_login.py) fails until you do. ## Database access for desktop users -----DATA --- # Data model Alloq stores its data in PostgreSQL. The tables are mapped by SQLAlchemy entities in [`alloq_commons/entities/`](../../components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/entities/__init__.py). The package exports 13 entities. The schema itself is created by the hand-written Alembic migrations in `alembic/versions/`, so a change to an entity always needs a migration as well (see [layers](./layers.md#migration)). Every entity inherits `Entity` from appkit-commons. `Entity` adds three columns that the tables below do not repeat: - `id`, integer primary key with autoincrement and an index. - `created`, timestamp with time zone, set by the database on insert. - `updated`, timestamp with time zone, set on insert and on every update. The same database also holds the appkit-user tables (`auth_users`, `auth_sessions`, `auth_oauth_accounts`, `auth_oauth_states` and others). They belong to appkit-user and are not described here. Alloq stores its app roles `project_manager` and `employee` in the roles list of the appkit user, not in the `roles` table below. See [security and access](./security-and-access.md). ## Entity relationship diagram ![Entity relationship diagram of the database](../diagrams/data-model.drawio.png) [Editable source: data-model.drawio](https://github.com/jenreh/alloq/blob/main/docs/diagrams/data-model.drawio) The diagram shows the relations only. The fields are in the tables below. `daily_rate_settings` and `public_holidays` have no foreign keys. ## How the planning data fits together Three tables describe the staffing of a project. They answer different questions. - `required_capacities` says how many person days of a role a project needs in total. It is meant to hold one row per project and role, but no unique constraint in the database enforces this. - `capacity_allocations` is the weekly plan. The stories come from the code at v2.0.4. Each story lives on a feature page, and the map links to it. The map shows titles only. The acceptance criteria and the evidence are on the feature pages. ## Vision and goals Alloq helps a software team plan which people work on which project in each week. It counts the free capacity of each person after absences, public holidays, part time and internal work, and it shows the state of the project portfolio. Alloq has four personas. Their goals come from the README and from the "so that" part of the stories. **Administrator.** - Decide who can sign in and what each person may read or change. - Keep the roles, daily rates, departments and public holidays that the planning and the prices use. - Give desktop users access to the central database. **Project manager.** - Plan people on projects week by week without overbooking anyone. - Keep the data, status and risks of each project current. - See the schedule, budget, risks and staffing gaps of the portfolio on one page. **Employee.** - Read the planning and the projects without changing them. - Keep their own account and password up to date. **Desktop user.** - Use Alloq as a macOS app with the Microsoft account, on the same central database, with no secret stored in the app. ## How to read the map - **Activities.** The big steps of the user journey, from left to right in the order a new team uses Alloq. Each activity has one or two feature pages. - **User tasks.** The columns of each table. A user task is something a person does, named from their point of view. - **Sub-tasks.** Smaller steps and variants under a user task. They are not columns, but each story belongs to one. The desktop app does not create users. An unknown email gives the message in `NO_ACCOUNT`, e.g. "Für {email} gibt es kein alloq-Konto. ..." [there is no alloq account for this email]. An inactive or not verified account gives the matching text from `STATUS_MESSAGES`. 6. The handler opens the normal appkit session with `_create_session` and redirects to the page the user asked for, or to the homepage. There is no password login in the desktop app. The docstring of `login_state.py` gives the reason: without a signed-in Microsoft account the app has no database access to check a password against. ### Token renewal and restart - `EntraSignIn` keeps the access token with its expiry. A background thread renews it `REFRESH_MARGIN` (300) seconds before it expires. When renewal fails, it tries again after `RETRY_SECONDS` (60) seconds. - `access_token()` never hands out a token that expires within `EXPIRY_SLACK` (60) seconds. - After a restart, `restore()` brings back the Microsoft account from the Keychain without a browser, as soon as a connection needs it. It tries at most every `RESTORE_INTERVAL` (30) seconds. When the Alloq session is still valid, the user goes on without the login page. ### Sign-out "Abmelden" [sign out] calls `DesktopLoginState.sign_out`. It ends the appkit session (`logout`), removes the Microsoft account from the token cache on this Mac (`EntraSignIn.sign_out`) and closes all database connections (`reset_connections`). ## Schema check [`app/desktop/schema.py`](../../app/desktop/schema.py) holds `KNOWN_REVISIONS`, the Alembic history newest first. `EXPECTED_REVISION` is the first entry. `schema_problem` reads `alembic_version` and returns: - `None` when the database has the expected revision. - A message that the server migration is still missing, when the revision is an older known one. - A message to update the app, when the revision is unknown or empty. After every new migration, add its revision at the front of `KNOWN_REVISIONS`. content.text:
All ten diagrams are redrawn in a typical developer-docs style, with content taken from the doc pages. I removed one duplicate diagram from the overview page. I checked every render visually, and nothing is committed.

**Style:** white background, light grey frames for groups, white cards with a thin colored bar and a small type label (for example "CONTAINER · PYTHON"). Code names are in a monospace font, Entra ID and PostgreSQL use the official Azure icons, and connectors are neutral grey. There are no title banners, because the page heading already names each diagram.

**Matched to the doc:**
- **Sequence diagrams:** the numbered badges on the messages match the numbered steps in the text. The projects page uses steps 2, 3 and 5–7, and desktop sign-in uses steps 1–6. The "no cached account" case sits in an `opt` frame.
- **Layers:** the diagram now branches. State goes both to Models and to the Repository, as the original Mermaid diagram showed. My earlier versions drew one straight chain, which was wrong.
- **Data model:** it shows only the relations, as the page says, using crow's-foot line ends. Lines to projects, employees and roles each have their own color, explained in a legend.
- **Story map:** each of the 118 stories is counted under its activity and task, taken from the map tables. The diagram shows the counts instead of repeating the story titles.

**Duplications removed:**
- In `overview.md`, the `alloq-system.svg` embed and its sentence showed the same containers as the deployment diagram above them. It also had facts the doc doesn't, like Docker port 8080 and PostgreSQL 15. I removed the embed but left the file in `docs/images`.
- Inside the diagrams, I dropped the parts the text next to them already says: the "Rules" panel, the "Key facts" panel, the guard callout, the layer descriptions (the layers table has them) and the "How to read" card.

The generator scripts are in my scratchpad, not in the repo. I saved this style to memory for future diagram work.
